name: Gevo, Inc.

profile.description: Gevo, Inc. (Englewood, Colorado) develops low-carbon fuels and carbon businesses: it owns Gevo North Dakota, a low-carbon ethanol plant with carbon capture and sequestration, sells carbon credits and Section 45Z tax credits, operates renewable natural gas assets, and is developing the ATJ-30 alcohol-to-jet sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) project in North Dakota [1][4]. FY2025 revenue was $160.6M, up from $16.9M in 2024 after the North Dakota acquisition [4]. Q2 2026 revenue was ~$47M with a $176M non-cash impairment tied to exiting the South Dakota ATJ-60 project, while the 2026 adjusted EBITDA target was raised to more than $60M [1]. Founder Patrick Gruber became Executive Chair and Paul Bloom became CEO in 2026 [2]. The stock trades at $1.25 (52-week range $1.09-$2.97), ~$309M market cap [4].

innovation.label: DEVELOPING
innovation.analysis: Track Record (2/3): Gevo pivoted from pre-revenue SAF development to an operating carbon-capture ethanol and carbon-credit business via the North Dakota acquisition, lifting revenue from $16.9M (2024) to $160.6M (2025) and guiding 2026 adjusted EBITDA above $60M [4][1]. AI Deployment (0/2): No AI products or quantified AI savings were found [1][2]. Market Share (1/2): Gevo is an early mover in CCS-enabled low-carbon ethanol and carbon credits, but it is a small participant in ethanol and SAF without category-leading share data [1]. Product Pipeline (1/2): The ATJ-30 project (convert ~50mmgpy ethanol to ~30mmgpy SAF) has completed FEL-3 engineering and debottlenecking targets 75mmgpy ethanol in 2026, but final investment decision and financing remain open [1]. R&D Intensity (1/1): TTM R&D is 5.7% of revenue, above specialty chemicals and fuels peers [4].

inspiration.label: WEAK
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (3/4): Gevo's long-held purpose of commercializing renewable hydrocarbon fuels with a net-zero lifecycle carbon footprint is specific and has guided the company for nearly two decades under founder Patrick Gruber [2][1]. Community Impact (0/2): No distinctive charitable or community investment program with dollar amounts was found [3]. Employee Retention (0/2): No tenure or turnover data was found; the few Comparably reviews are mixed and critical of leadership [2]. Insider Buying (0/2): FMP insider statistics show 2 open-market purchases against 37 insider sales from Q4 2025 through Q3 2026, i.e. net selling [4].

infrastructure.label: DEVELOPING
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored as a Growth stock. D/E of 62.5% scores 1.0, and the 2020-2025 revenue CAGR of ~96% (acquisition-driven, $5.5M to $160.6M) scores 1.0 at 2x weight [4]. Q2 2026 revenue growth of 7.1% YoY scores 0.90 [4]. TTM ROE of -51.4% (2x weight) and TTM net margin of -119.9% both score 0, driven by the $176M Q2 impairment [4][1]. FY2027 consensus EPS is about -$0.002, so forward P/E is negative and scores 0 [4]. PEG is excluded as not meaningful with negative trailing and forward earnings (FMP's 0.02 reading is an artifact of loss-based math), leaving 8 weight units; weighted 3.90/8 = 4.88, rounding to 5. Liquidity passes at ~2.9M shares/day (~$3.6M daily).

ai_resilience.label: LOW RISK
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (8/9): IMMUNE. Gevo produces physical fuels (ethanol, RNG, future SAF), sequesters CO2 underground and monetizes regulatory credits (45Z, Canada Clean Fuel Regulation), none of which AI can substitute [1]. No analyst commentary flags AI as a risk; the business's swing factors are policy, commodity spreads and project financing. AI Opportunity (0/1): No AI-related revenue [1].

infinite_game.summary: Gevo has pursued one cause, decarbonizing liquid fuels, for nearly two decades and has completed an orderly founder-to-successor CEO transition [2]. Through Sinek's lens the story is mixed: the cause is genuine and has driven repeated reinvention, but many pivots (isobutanol chemicals, South Dakota SAF, now North Dakota CCS and credits) were forced by capital and policy constraints, the latest ending in a $176M write-off, and there is little evidence of a high-trust culture [1][2].

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (2/3): Replacing fossil hydrocarbons with net-zero renewable fuels is idealistic, service-oriented and larger than any single product, and has held since Gruber took over in 2007 [2]. It remains unproven commercially and highly dependent on subsidies, so it is not yet a validated competitive advantage.

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): Management chose to write off $176M of ATJ-60 development costs and exit Lake Preston, South Dakota to concentrate SAF in North Dakota where carbon capture is already operating, a costly but disciplined decision [1]. It also reflects earlier capital allocation that did not work, so it is one example rather than a pattern.

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (1/2): Succession was handled internally, with President Paul Bloom (five years at Gevo, ex-ADM) succeeding founder Patrick Gruber, who stays as Executive Chair [2]. Small-sample Comparably reviews are critical of leadership, and no retention data exists, so trust is adequate rather than high.

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): Gevo has moved from isobutanol renewable chemicals to SAF development to an operating ethanol-plus-carbon-capture and carbon-credit business, now centred on North Dakota [1][4]. These shifts serve the decarbonization cause but were largely driven by financing and policy necessity rather than chosen from strength.

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): No management commentary was found framing competitors (other SAF developers, ethanol producers with CCS) as worthy rivals that drive self-improvement [1].

investment_thesis: Gevo has become an operating business: the North Dakota ethanol-plus-carbon-capture plant lifted FY2025 revenue to $160.6M, Q2 2026 adjusted EBITDA was $11M, and management more than doubled its 2026 adjusted EBITDA target to over $60M on a new Canada Clean Fuel Regulation pathway and more than $70M of expected Section 45Z tax credit monetization [4][1]. The ATJ-30 SAF project has completed FEL-3 engineering and debottlenecking targets 75mmgpy of low-carbon ethanol [1]. At $1.25 the stock trades near book value (P/B 1.08) and ~1.7x sales, and its Inspire Impact Score of 61 (ALIGNED) has no negative attributions [4].
thesis_continued: The bear case is that Gevo's economics rest on policy. Profits depend on 45Z credits, low-carbon fuel standards and carbon-credit pricing that can change with administrations, and analysts expect roughly breakeven EPS through 2028 (FY2027 consensus about -$0.002) [4]. The Q2 2026 GAAP loss of $177M from the ATJ-60 impairment shows the cost of past capital allocation, cash was about $58M at quarter-end, and ATJ-30 still needs financing and an FID [1]. Insiders have been net sellers, and the stock is near its 52-week low of $1.09 [4].
key_catalysts: Q3 2026 results expected to include the first Canada Clean Fuel Regulation credit revenue, supporting the raised >$60M 2026 adjusted EBITDA target [1]
Monetization of more than $70M of Section 45Z clean fuel production tax credits in 2026, including $16M received after Q2 [1]
Final investment decision and financing for ATJ-30 SAF in North Dakota, building on completed FEL-3 engineering and 2026 ethanol debottlenecking to 75mmgpy [1]
key_risks: Policy dependence: earnings hinge on 45Z credits, low-carbon fuel standards and voluntary carbon markets; adverse changes could erase the projected EBITDA [1]
Capital intensity and dilution risk: ~$58M cash against SAF project needs, after a $176M impairment on the abandoned ATJ-60 project [1]
Persistent GAAP losses (TTM net margin -120%, ROE -51%) and consensus EPS near zero through 2028 leave little earnings support for the equity [4]
